title: Light and Optics
scopeNote: Original condensed MCAT Physics, Mathematics and Research Reasoning lessons. Models and calculations use stated assumptions. Independent scientific review is pending; this is not exhaustive textbook coverage.

steps.text: Electromagnetic waves in vacuum travel at c and obey c = fλ. The spectrum orders radio, microwave, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-ray and gamma-ray regions by increasing typical frequency.
A photon has energy E = hf = hc/λ. Greater frequency means greater energy per photon; greater intensity can instead mean more photons arriving per time and area.

In a material, phase speed and wavelength can change while the frequency from a steady source remains fixed at a stationary boundary. The vacuum c relation does not use the material wavelength unchanged.
Spectrum bands are useful categories rather than perfectly universal origin-free boundaries. A wave’s speed in vacuum does not increase because its frequency is higher.

steps.text: In the thin-lens model, 1/f = 1/do + 1/di. Use a consistent sign convention: a converging lens has positive f, a real object has positive do, and a real image has positive di.
Transverse magnification is m = -di/do in this convention. Negative m means an inverted image; positive m means an upright image.
Snell’s law uses n1 sin θ1 = n2 sin θ2 with angles measured from the normal. Total internal reflection requires travel from higher n to lower n and an angle beyond the critical value.
A ray sketch constrains image location and orientation. Thin-lens equations require the stated approximation and do not model every thick lens or aberration.

steps.text: Diffraction spreads waves passing through openings or around edges. It becomes prominent when the opening size is comparable to wavelength.
For a single slit of width a, minima satisfy a sin θ = mλ for nonzero integers m. A narrower slit gives a broader central maximum for a fixed wavelength.
Two-slit interference and single-slit diffraction have different formulas and meanings. Do not call a single-slit minimum a two-slit bright fringe.
The small-angle approximation sin θ ≈ tan θ ≈ y/L uses angles in radians and requires a suitable geometry. Real patterns can combine interference with a diffraction envelope.

steps.text: Polarization specifies the orientation pattern of an electromagnetic wave’s electric field. Longitudinal sound in air does not have the same transverse polarization freedom.
An ideal polarizer transmits half the intensity of unpolarized incident light. For already linearly polarized light, Malus’s law gives I = I0 cos² θ relative to the transmission axis.
Two ideal crossed polarizers transmit zero of an initially transmitted linear polarization. Adding an intermediate polarizer can change that result by changing the transmitted polarization direction.
Intensity is not electric-field amplitude: intensity is proportional to amplitude squared in a fixed medium. A one-half amplitude ratio gives a one-quarter intensity ratio.
